summary: Worst-case legal inputs have four letter choices at every digit, and the required result materializes every length-n combination, so the output lower bound already matches the backtracking upper bound.

optimality.argument: For an input made only of 7 and 9, the result contains exactly 4^n distinct strings of length n. Returning that list requires Omega(n * 4^n) character materialization, while the depth-first search visits each combination once and joins exactly n path characters at each leaf.

replacement_checks.evidence: A worst-case input has 4^n required outputs, each containing n characters, so any eager implementation must materialize Omega(n * 4^n) output characters.
The candidate explores one tree edge per chosen letter, reuses an n-character path, and performs one O(n) join for each of at most 4^n leaves.

An independent Cartesian-product oracle checks every legal digit string of lengths 1 through 4 against the app-local and immutable native implementations; the candidate is checked through the same complete domain.
